editorial: Way Down East is a 1920 American silent melodrama produced and directed by D. W. Griffith and released through United Artists, starring Lillian Gish and Richard Barthelmess. Adapted from Lottie Blair Parker's stage play, it was one of the highest-grossing films of the silent era and is famous for its climactic ice-floe rescue. Published in 1920, the film print's 75-year US copyright term has expired, placing the photoplay in the public domain by term expiry.
